name: Shaker object
region: Shaker villages of New England and New York, United States
summary: The plain household goods of the Shaker communities: ladder-back chairs, peg rails, oval boxes and chests of pine, maple and cherry, built for use with no applied ornament.

philosophy.core_thesis: An object that serves its use well is beautiful; the maker adds no ornament, shows each joint and makes each piece with honest care.
design_principles: Make each object for its use; remove each part that has no job.
Use thin, light parts: a chair post of 25 to 32 mm and a rail of 12 to 20 mm.
Show the joint: a dovetail, a mortise or a tenon stays in view.
Use wood in a plain finish: oil, wax or a thin matte paint in red, yellow, blue or green.
Hang each chair on a peg rail of 7 to 9 cm pegs, so that the floor is free for the broom.
Make a box or a drawer in 3 to 7 sizes that nest, with swallowtail fingers of thin maple.
Keep the line straight and the turning simple: a ball finial and a taper are the only decoration.

form.geometry: Straight lines, rectangles and ovals; the round peg, the tapered post and the oval band are the only curves.
form.silhouette: A light, upright outline with open space: a tall narrow chair with 3 to 4 slats, and a plain box case on a thin frame.
form.edges: A small, hand-softened edge of 1 to 3 mm; no moulding and no bead.
form.proportion: A ladder-back chair is about 100 cm high with a seat at 43 cm; a post is about 1/4 as thick as it is wide in the seat.
form.ornament: None. A ball finial on a chair post, and a tapered foot, are the only added forms.
rules: Each joint is a plain mortise, tenon or dovetail, and stays in view.
A seat is woven of cotton tape, cane or rush, in 1 or 2 colours.
Each part is as thin as its load allows; a post is 25 to 32 mm.
A painted surface is a matte, flat colour; a bare surface has an oil or wax finish.

materials.rule: Local wood makes about 80% of the object; metal is only a hinge, a stove or a sconce, and cloth is plain tape or wool.

finish.gloss: 2–15 GU on wood and paint; 5–25 GU on iron
finish.patina: The style welcomes a soft, even wear on wood, a scrubbed pale top and a paint that thins on the edges.

hardware.section: Pegs 25–30 mm; stems and rods 6–12 mm; a hinge 3 mm thick
hardware.joints: Plain dovetails, mortises and tenons in view; wooden pegs and small cut nails.
hardware.handles: A small turned wooden knob of 25 to 30 mm, or a plain wooden peg.
hardware.switches_and_taps: Before 1880 there is no electric switch; the period-faithful reissue is a cotton-braided cable with a plain wooden turn switch. A tap is a plain iron or brass cock over a stone basin.

palette.strategy: The colour of bare wood, with a thin, flat paint in the Shaker red, yellow, blue and green, and a cream wall.

processes: shop production in the community workshops
manufacture.scale: Community workshops made chairs and boxes in series of 10s to 1000s for sale to the public.
manufacture.signs: A tight dovetail, a swallowtail finger on a band, an even taper on a post and a woven tape seat.

objects.form: stoneware wash basin on a plain stand
cotton-braided flex with a plain turn switch (a period-faithful reissue)
hanging tin sconce on a peg rail
rocking armchair with a tape seat and a ball finial
ladder-back chair with a woven tape seat
oval box of thin maple with swallowtail fingers

positive: ladder-back chair with woven tape seat
thin matte paint in red and blue
studio product photograph, soft north light

evidence.title: Shaker rocking chair at Pleasant Hill

emotion.target_response: Quiet calm and trust in a modest, useful object: the viewer feels that nothing is false or extra.

use_cases: a plain, handmade kitchen or hall
a reissue of a peg rail, a box or a chair
a still life of useful objects
a hardware schedule for a farmhouse
avoid_when: The brief asks for gloss, glamour or ornament.
The room needs soft, deep upholstery.

modifiers.how: Change to mahogany with a French polish, add flutes and brass mounts.
Keep the oak and the exposed joint, and add hammered copper, a stylised leaf and a wool rug.
Use pale ash and birch, thinner parts, and wool in natural white.

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.
